grade.first_issue: No decisive defect. The brief argument that zero nonunit entries cannot remain is valid when combined with the fact that every legal move starts with at least two entries greater than 1 and decreases their number by at most one.
grade.summary: The proof is complete and correct. The lexicographically decreasing pair consisting of the total prime-exponent sum and the number of entries greater than 1 proves termination. A legal move cannot eliminate all entries greater than 1. Primewise, the gcd of all valuations is invariant under the Euclidean-algorithm transformation, and at a terminal board this invariant equals the valuation of the unique remaining integer, determining it independently of all choices.
strengths: Correctly identifies a well-founded lexicographic measure for termination and treats both gcd cases.
Correctly proves preservation of the primewise gcd of valuations, including zero valuations.
Derives an explicit formula for the terminal integer solely from the initial board.
